votes.reason: JNJ qualifies: its 26-week channel rises 40% a year and its weekly MACD histogram is rising above zero, and although 0.9 widths above the line is not a pullback entry, the trend and momentum give no reason against holding it.

CVX only just qualifies, with a channel rising 1% a year, but its weekly MACD histogram is rising above zero, so sitting 1.5 widths above the line makes it a stretched entry rather than a pullback, not a falling or broken chart.

PGR fails my test because its 40-week average is not rising, and although it sits right on the line (0.1 widths below) of a channel rising 27% a year, its weekly MACD histogram is falling, so momentum has not turned up.

LMT's 26-week channel slopes down 15% a year and its weekly MACD histogram is still falling, so whatever caused the recent drop, the chart shows a falling trend with no turn in momentum rather than a pullback in a rising channel.

CAT is the exact setup I look for: it has pulled back to 1.3 widths below the line of a 26-week channel rising 40% a year, well short of the 2.5-width break, and its weekly MACD histogram is already turning up above zero.
